chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) it was said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isحاق ibn 'Ammar, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

He said: 'Indeed, the place of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) has a known sanctity; whoever knows it and seeks refuge in it is granted refuge.' I said: 'Describe its place for me, may I be your ransom.' He said: 'Wipe/rub from the place of his grave today twenty-five cubits from in front of it, and twenty-five cubits from near his head, and twenty-five cubits from the side of his feet, and twenty-five cubits from behind it. And the place of his grave, from the day he was buried, is a meadow from the meadows of Paradise, and from it is a ladder by which the deeds of its visitors are ascended to the sky. So there is no angel in the sky nor in the earth except that they ask Allah for the visitation of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). A group descends and a group ascends.'
ai.seo_question: What are the dimensions and spiritual significance of Imam al-Husayn's grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the sacred boundaries of Imam al-Husayn’s grave, establishing a 25-cubit radius in all directions as a zone of asylum (*istijara*) for those who seek refuge. The narration elevates the site to a 'meadow of Paradise' (*rawdatun min riad al-jannah*), serving as a spiritual ascension point where angels on earth and in heaven intercede for the visitors, highlighting the cosmological significance of Karbala in Shia piety.
